title: When Returns Sound Too Good, They Usually Are
summary: Fraudulent schemes often advertise steady, unusually high payouts that never seem to have a losing period — a pattern real markets do not produce.
blocks: Fraudulent schemes often advertise steady, unusually high payouts that never seem to have a losing period — a pattern real markets do not produce.
Many operate as Ponzi structures, paying earlier participants with the deposits of newer ones until the flow of new money stops and the whole thing collapses.
Steady, outsized, risk-free-sounding payouts are the classic warning sign. Genuine markets move up and down; certainty is the sales pitch of a scam.
